conclusions: Rounding absolute coordinates during PG preparation is a material contributor to hv influence error. Holding already-PG-rounded coordinates fixed leaves the near-gate residual; higher precision before that rounding changes it substantially.

The requested float64 subtract-before-PG form reduces maximum hv coefficient error against 80-digit reference by 37.4x and 217.3x for the two saved cases. Gamma-weighted hv error improves 56.9x and 104.4x. The largest cp error is unchanged; no every-entry improvement is claimed.
The residual of the fixed saved state moves in both directions under improved arithmetic. This does not establish a converged equilibrium or justify changing any acceptance threshold.

Earlier geometry realization is another material precision layer: extended full geometry/orientation yields circulation maxima 2.4443e-12 and 4.5684e-12 at these same stored states. A local float64 anchor is not a universal repair, despite improving some near-anchor coordinates.

Evidence supports a principled, algebraically identical relative-PG arithmetic candidate. General source/tangent/cache/ground regression and any later nonlinear replay are separate work; this report changes no production code.
limitations: Source and state inputs are already float64. Extended arithmetic cannot recover source values beyond their stored precision.
No influence geometry, wake/core model, stiffness, mass, density, gravity, tolerance or measured target was fitted.
No new equilibrium, stability result or experimental comparison is produced.
